x: The Boys Competition was won by newcomer P.Smith who was the only Boy to collect points in each of the minimum of five events.

Particular mention ought to be made of the fact that Cocks has gained his Senior bedge whilst a Junior and also his Junior Standard whilst only a Youth. At this stage too, the Boys and Youths medal competition awards were made to P.

Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major. Many others who are under the guidance of Tom Carter are improving fast and the seniors will surely benefit in the very near future.

Chris Martin put up a couple of really good times in the sprints, winning the 220y and placing 2nd in the 100y. In the quarter mile Philip Smith recorded a personal best and with a little more experience should improve this time even further.
Phil Smith improved yet again in the 'quarter' - this time to 53.9 . He has proved to himself that regular training pays off so lets hope he keeps up the hard work.

Great backing by Derek Hurd (who seems to be finding his old form) and quarter-miler Philip Smith (he could never have dreamed of winning his first County medal in a cross country race) ensured us of a suprise 2nd place in the team event.

This,incidentally, is 39 secs. faster than John Bicourt's winning time in the Surrey Championship over the same course, less approx. 75 yards at the finish. That surfin',hammer throwing,vodka drinking,half-miler - John Kelly was 2nd in 33:37 and Phil Smith 3rd, 13 seconds later.

Adrian Major improved on his best half mile clocking as did Philip Smith in the'quarter', but the hardest worked athlete of the meeting was John Thresher who took the 2 miles in 9:03.1 and no more than 10 minutes later lined up for the mile , this time finishing 2nd.
Behind him were two more "p.b's" -L.Mann (2:00.4), Tony Fairclough(2:03.5) . Laurie O'Hara won the 2 miles as he liked from a large field whilst Philip Smith improved to 53.0 in the 440yds.

Another three-tenths of a second came off for Philip Smith in the 440yds with 52.4 . Steadily removing chunks off his best time, Philip could go faster still this season from the way he finished this race.

Philip Smith was very pleased with his 10.7 - as he should be. Anthony Heath won his second mile in Belgrave colours with 4:21.9 but only after Alan Black inexplicably dropped out whilst in the lead with only 220 yards left.
Youth John Kelly was 2nd after running the entire race on his own, followed home three-quarters of a minute later by Phil Smith who ran extremely well to beat Derek Hurd.

Thresher's mile win was a track record and Philip Smith's 3rd place in the 'B' 440yds was a personal best. Amongst the Juniors Tony Brooks scored a large percentage of our points and Steve White, only a Youth, took the two 'A' sprints by impressive margins.
Also the indefatigable Bob Taylor and Gwen Cousins plus the welcome recruits Peter Hillier and friend, Philip Smith and friend and John Hall and Marjorie Pearson and Bob Glover.
Philip Smith and Cliff Brooks are both capable of pushing any of this quartet and if any of our talented sprinters turned their hand to some over-distance work, who knows what might happen.
Otherwise, we had sound and loyal contributions from Tony Brooks, Philip Gee, Philip Smith and Dave Rees (a startling improvement to sub-55 by Dave).

On the sidelines will be DAVE [illegible]EES and CLIFF BROOKS while I cannot be certain of PHILIP SMITH'S fitness at the moment, if he knuckles down to hard training he will also be a useful substitute.

Our old friend George Flanagan made a re-appearance in 14th place - but his allowance of only 400 yards seems to indicate a long memory on the part of the handicapper. Philip Smith's seven yards enabled him to hold off Cliff Brooks in the 120 yards.
